name: AMANDA
full_name: Antarctic Muon And Neutrino Detector Array
summary: Historical ice-neutrino-array precursor to IceCube, searching for neutrinos from dark-matter annihilation in the Sun and Earth's core.
physics_targets: WIMP capture in the Sun / Earth
detection_principle: Optical modules record Cherenkov light from upward-going muons in ice; event counts toward the Sun / Earth's core relative to atmospheric backgrounds set limits.

sites.name: Beneath the ice at the South Pole station
sites.location: Beneath the ice at the South Pole station

status.label: Data taking ended / historical experiment
status.evidence: Collaboration papers record joint AMANDA / IceCube operation until 2009.

key_parameters.name: AMANDA-II
key_parameters.value: 19 strings, 677 modules, at about 1.5–2 km depth

phases.name: AMANDA-II
phases.description: 19 strings and later joint operation with IceCube

results.summary: Multiyear solar searches constrain neutralino scenarios over 50–5000 GeV.

science_scope: Tests dark-matter models through astrophysical radiation, cosmic rays or neutrinos. Astrophysical backgrounds and propagation models affect interpretation; an anomaly alone does not establish dark matter.
